channel.title: Calamares 3.3.14 segfault during manual partitioning (Lenovo Slim Pro X 14ARH7 / Ryzen 9 6900HS)
channel.description:
AI helped a bit in identifying this. Am i only supposed to do full disk erasure? thx!
**Environment**
* ISO: Kicksecure-LXQt-18.2.4.2.Intel_AMD64.iso (OpenPGP-verified) * Boot method: Ventoy USB, GRUB → "LIVE Mode | SYSMAINT Session" → Install System * Hardware: Lenovo Slim Pro X 14ARH7, AMD Ryzen 9 6900HS (Rembrandt), Samsung PM9A1 1TB NVMe + Nividia igpu * Target disk already contains another Linux install (Ubuntu) with existing ESP; installing into unallocated free space
**Steps to reproduce**
1. Launch installer from live session 2. Manual partitioning on `/dev/nvme0n1` 3. Create new partitions in existing free space (\~96GB): ext4 `/boot` (5GB), LUKS2 root (80GB), fat32 ESP (10GB), plus a small swap; existing ESP assigned to `/boot/efi` (not reformatted) 4. Begin install
**Result (100% reproducible, 3/3 attempts)**
`Starting job "Create new 80000MiB partition on /dev/nvme0n1" (5 / 33) /usr/bin/install-host-calamares-wrapper: line 31: Segmentation fault (core dumped) calamares -D8 ## ERROR detected! ## BASH_COMMAND: sudo --non-interactive --preserve-env install-host-calamares-wrapper ## Please report this bug! `
The crash occurs at the first partition-creation job, before any partition modifications complete. No error popup from the GUI — only the terminal wrapper output. After the crash the live desktop also exhibits intermittent UI stalls.
**Additional info**
* `session.log` and the complete install-host output available on request * Calamares reports: version 3.3.14, Qt 6.8.2, backend plugin "pmsfdiskbackendplugin"

item.title: Calamares 3.3.14 segfault during manual partitioning (Lenovo Slim Pro X 14ARH7 / Ryzen 9 6900HS)
item.dc:creator: arraybolt3
item.description:
Some of the screens are missing which makes it a bit hard to tell what’s happening, but:

  1. Are you sure your system is actually a UEFI system? You probably already know this, but there are two major firmware types used by most PCs, BIOS (older) and UEFI (newer).
  2. If your previous OS install didn’t have an EFI system partition, you’re using a BIOS system, and should NOT create a UEFI partition at all. If your system does have an EFI partition, do NOT create a new one, instead tell Calamares to reuse the existing one without reformatting it.

That might resolve the problem.

If the issue really is that you can’t create new LUKS partitions alongside existing ones, then you may have to use the erase disk option. I somewhat doubt this is the issue though. Will try to reproduce.

item.title: Calamares 3.3.14 segfault during manual partitioning (Lenovo Slim Pro X 14ARH7 / Ryzen 9 6900HS)
item.dc:creator: kicksecure.jr6xp
item.description:
@arraybolt3 used ai to do some troubleshooting.

could this be the issue and some solutions?? or s omething else?

The Calamares LUKS/partition-creation segfault — known, widespread, with workarounds

This class of bug isn’t limited to Kicksecure; it appears across distros that ship Calamares with the sfdisk backend, especially in manual partitioning + LUKS scenarios:

Upstream bug trackers:

  • Codeberg Calamares #2426 — “Segmentation fault while creating LUKS partitions” (the exact crash: installer dies at partition-creation job) → #2426 - Segmentation fault while creating LUKS partitions - Calamares/calamares - Codeberg.org
  • Codeberg Calamares #2454 — “Replace Partition” splits partitions incorrectly with separate /boot (Calamares forces a new /boot + LUKS split even when one exists; workaround: delete existing /boot and LUKS first) → #2454 - "Replace Partion" Issues with Separate /boot - Calamares/calamares - Codeberg.org

Reports on other distros (same backend, same symptom):

  • Manjaro: installer stops/crashes making a LUKS partition — Manjaro Installer Stops After Trying to Make a LUKS Partition - Support - Manjaro Linux Forum
  • Manjaro: Calamares crashes entering custom partitioning — Calamares crashes upon entering the custom disk partitioning section - Support - Manjaro Linux Forum
  • Manjaro: encryption partition bugs (formatting an existing LUKS/ext4 partition never offers the encrypt option) — Problem with calamares and partition encryption - Support - Manjaro Linux Forum
  • Nitrux: “fails to create new partitions” — Calamares fails to create new partitions when selecting 'Replace partition' · Issue #55 · Nitrux/nitrux-bug-tracker · GitHub

Workarounds people actually use successfully:

  1. Pre-create all partitions outside Calamares (parted/cryptsetup/mkfs from a live session or GParted), then in Calamares only assign mount points to existing partitions — the buggy create-partition job never runs. This is the most-cited reliable workaround across the threads above.
  2. Delete the pre-existing LUKS//boot partitions first, then use guided modes (“Replace a partition” / “Erase disk”) — guided paths bypass manual-mode bugs (per Codeberg #2454 and the Manjaro threads).
  3. Skip Calamares entirely — some users install the underlying distro via its non-Calamares installer (e.g., Debian’s debian-installer) or by-hand Arch-style, then use Kicksecure’s official Debian-morph path ( Install Kicksecure inside Debian ) to transform it into Kicksecure.
  4. Fresh-disk installs don’t hit it — the crash class is overwhelmingly “manual partitions + existing LUKS/dual-boot disk”; Erase Disk on an empty drive generally works.

Root cause area (for devs): the KPMCore pmsfdiskbackendplugin partition-creation path, and Calamares’s LUKS handling limitations (it also has documented weaknesses reusing existing LUKS partitions and separate /boot configurations, per the Calamares LUKS deployment wiki: Deploy LUKS · calamares/calamares Wiki · GitHub).

item.title: Calamares 3.3.14 segfault during manual partitioning (Lenovo Slim Pro X 14ARH7 / Ryzen 9 6900HS)
item.dc:creator: arraybolt3
item.description:
kicksecure.jr6xp:
  • Boot method: Ventoy USB

This might be a problem. Try using one of the USB drive preparation methods documented here:

Kicksecure – 15 May 26

2 Write the ISO to USB - Kicksecure Live ISO (via USB) and Installation

Kicksecure Installation Guide. This guide will help you download the ISO image, create your bootable media, and install Kicksecure on your computer.

After doing that, try to install again and see if you get better results.

kicksecure.jr6xp:

Starting job “Create new 80000MiB partition on /dev/nvme0n1” (5 / 33) /usr/bin/install-host-calamares-wrapper: line 31: Segmentation fault (core dumped) calamares -D8 ## ERROR detected! ## BASH_COMMAND: sudo --non-interactive --preserve-env install-host-calamares-wrapper ## Please report this bug!

There’s a chance you’re running into this bug, which only affects some hardware. If using an alternate flashing method doesn’t work, use the technique documented here to remove the gather_data_sampling=force kernel parameter while booting the live ISO:

Kicksecure – 13 May 26

Temporary Kernel Boot Parameter Change - grub bootloader Configuration Changes

Kernel Boot Parameter Changes

kicksecure.jr6xp:
  1. Create new partitions in existing free space (~96GB): ext4 /boot (5GB), LUKS2 root (80GB), fat32 ESP (10GB), plus a small swap; existing ESP assigned to /boot/efi (not reformatted)

This is a bit self-contradictory; your partition sizes sum up to about 96 GB but you say you’re both creating an EFI system partition and that you’re reusing an old one. Which is it?

(Also, 10 GB is massive for an EFI system partition… Kicksecure’s is 300 MB by default and even that’s mostly unused.)

Given your partition sizes, it looks like you’re using manual partitioning. If neither of the above fixes work, please list step by step exactly which buttons you click and in what order to create the manual partitioning layout you’re using, as this will probably be necessary to reproduce the issue, and we might notice something you’re clicking that’s incorrect. Screenshots would also be useful. Manual partitioning is rather fiddly and easy to get wrong.
